# Adjudication Task — Chapter 959

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃959화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|세상에 존재하는 모든 만물은 저마다의 색깔을 지니고 있고, 사람 역시 예외는 아니다.
  6|
  7|눈빛이, 표정이, 온몸을 둘러싼 특유의 기운이 누군가를 설명하고 증명한다.
  8|
  9|그리고 그런 의미에서, 진무경은 눈앞의 사내를 본 순간 본능적으로 깨달을 수밖에 없었다.
 10|
 11|‘마인(魔人).’
 12|
 13|머릿속을 스쳐 지나간 두 글자.
 14|
 15|틀림없었다.
 16|
 17|살기에 취해 있는 눈빛과 느슨하게 올라간 입꼬리.
 18|
 19|거기에 더해 사내의 전신에서 배어나는 혈향(血香)은 마주 선 것만으로도 코끝이 저릴 지경이었으니.
 20|
 21|‘이놈은…… 도대체 뭐지?’
 22|
 23|진무경은 가라앉은 눈빛으로 사내를 응시했다.
 24|
 25|이미 피부로 느꼈다. 머리로 이해했다.
 26|
 27|느닷없이 나타난 새로운 적이 평범한 악인(惡人)과는 차원이 다르다는 사실을.
 28|
 29|과거 항산검문을 기습하고, 생각지도 못한 무위로 그에게 상당한 내상을 안겨 주었던 적풍단주 풍양조차 저자에 비하면 일개 마적에 지나지 않는다고 생각될 정도였다.
 30|
 31|결이 다르고, 격이 다르다.
 32|
 33|지금껏 쌓아 올린 살업(殺業)은 물론, 일신의 무위(武威)까지도.
 34|
 35|그리고 그런 진무경을 바라보며, 칭겐은 씩 웃었다.
 36|
 37|“역시, 눈빛이 좋아.”
 38|
 39|저벅. 쉭!
 40|
 41|칭겐이 산책하듯 가볍게 발걸음을 내디딘 순간, 신형을 날려 뒤로 훌쩍 물러난 진무경이 비스듬히 검신을 곧추세웠다.
 42|
 43|“기감도 쓸 만하고.”
 44|
 45|칭겐이 만족스럽게 고개를 끄덕였다.
 46|
 47|아주 미세한 살기를 흘렸을 뿐이건만, 단 한 치의 망설임조차 없는 반응 속도.
 48|
 49|비록 적이기는 하나, 그는 눈앞의 젊은 검귀(劍鬼)가 생각 이상으로 썩 마음에 들었다.
 50|
 51|단순한 사냥감으로 생각하기에는 아까울 정도로.
 52|
 53|“분위기가 다 죽어 가는 늙은이처럼 어두컴컴하긴 해도 아직 한참 어린놈 같은데……. 너, 누구냐? 내 제자 할래?”
 54|
 55|그 누구도 예상치 못했던 한마디에, 칭겐의 등장으로 잠시 소강 상태에 빠져 있던 전장의 분위기가 술렁였다.
 56|
 57|그중에서도 특히 무너진 바위 틈새에서 신음하고 있던 백여 명의 유목민은 눈과 귀를 의심하며 자신들의 대족장을 부릅뜬 눈으로 바라보았다.
 58|
 59|테무르와 칭겐이 다스리는 서부 초원에 속한 그들은 두 젊은 대족장에 대해 잘 알고 있었고, 그렇기에 지금 이 상황이 더욱더 믿어지지 않았다.
 60|
 61|일신의 무위보다는 지략과 통치력으로 칸의 자리에 오른 칭겐이 그 비범한 무위를 통해 단신으로 초원의 형제들을 수백이나 도륙한 적에게 이런 제안을 하다니.
 62|
 63|“카, 칸이시여!”
 64|
 65|“이 무슨 말도 안 되는……!”
 66|
 67|사방에서 터져 나오는 경악 어린 외침.
 68|
 69|칭겐과 케식들의 등장에 기뻐하던 기색은 이미 한참 전에 사라졌다.
 70|
 71|각기 크고 작은 부상을 입은 채, 부릅뜬 눈으로 자신을 바라보는 유목민들의 모습에 칭겐이 입맛을 다셨다.
 72|
 73|“하긴, 역시 이런 상황에 제안하기엔 좀 많이 이상하지? 아직 주위에 보는 눈도 있고.”
 74|
 75|바로 그때였다.
 76|
 77|칭겐의 왼손에 들려 있던 소검(小劍)이 흐릿해진 것은.
 78|
 79|서걱, 쿠구궁!
 80|
 81|서늘한 절삭음과 함께 간신히 맞물린 채 쌓여 있던 바위 더미가 무너지며 유목민들을 덮쳤다.
 82|
 83|구조를 기다리던 그들의 비명이 굉음에 파묻히더니 이내 완전히 지워졌다.
 84|
 85|“하등 도움도 안 되는 쓸모없는 것들이, 하여간 말은 많아서 문제라니까.”
 86|
 87|“……!”
 88|
 89|“자, 이제 보는 눈이 없어졌으니 아까 하던 이야기나 마저 해 보자고. 응?”
 90|
 91|순간 내려앉은 정적 속, 깊숙이 가라앉은 눈빛으로 칭겐을 응시하던 진무경이 불현듯 입술을 뗐다.
 92|
 93|“칭겐이라고, 네놈이?”
 94|
 95|“어허, 네놈이라니?”
 96|
 97|작게 혀를 찬 칭겐이 말을 이었다.
 98|
 99|“아무리 애새끼라고 해도 그렇지, 스승님한테 못 하는 말이 없구나. 확 그냥 혓바닥을 뽑아 버릴라.”
100|
101|건들거리는 태도와 숨길 수 없는 강자의 여유.
102|
103|진무경은 유목민 특유의 변발을 한 눈앞의 사내가, 수많은 비밀로 이루어진 존재라는 것을 어렵지 않게 알아차릴 수 있었다.
104|
105|“역용(易用)을 했군. 진짜 칭겐은 어디에 있나?”
106|
107|곰곰이 생각하던 칭겐이 대답했다.
108|
109|“글쎄, 아마 지금쯤이면 독수리 배 속이 아닐까?”
110|
111|“또 다른 한 명은?”
112|
113|“다른 한 명? 아, 테무르 그놈은 살려 뒀지. 둘 중 하나는 살려 둬야 서부 놈들을 제대로 통제할 수 있으니까.”
114|
115|칭겐은 거리낌 없이 대꾸했다.
116|
117|어차피 반경 수십여 장은 케식이 통제하고 있는 상황.
118|
119|자무카가 오랜 세월 공들여 키워 낸 친위대인 그들은 결코 주인을 배반하지 않는다.
120|
121|그 어떤 흉포한 사냥개라도 제 주인은 물지 않듯이.
122|
123|“뭐, 이 정도면 네 궁금증은 충분히 해결해 준 것 같은데……. 이 몸의 관대한 제의는 어떻게 생각하나?”
124|
125|칭겐이 몹시 기대하는 눈빛으로 진무경을 바라본 그 순간.
126|
127|“불가(不可).”
128|
129|낮게 깔린 목소리가 불쑥 울려 퍼졌다.
130|
131|진무경의 어깨 너머로 보이는 한 사람의 얼굴에 칭겐이 눈살을 찌푸렸다.
132|
133|“안 된다니, 어째서? 아니, 그 전에 네놈이 뭔데?”
134|
135|이야기를 방해한 불청객이 담담하게 대꾸했다.
136|
137|“늑대가 어떻게 개새끼 밑으로 들어가겠나. 친자식처럼 애지중지 키운 아우인데, 형님으로서 그런 꼴은 못 보지.”
138|
139|“아우? 형님?”
140|
141|살짝 커진 눈으로 불청객, 진위경을 바라보던 칭겐이 피식 웃었다.
142|
143|“진씨 형제라……. 이거, 생각보다 훨씬 큰 월척이 걸려들었네.”
144|
145|월척.
146|
147|그 두 글자에 진위경의 눈빛이 무거워졌다.
148|
149|전투가 벌어지기 전, 월척을 낚아 오겠다며 껄껄 웃던 늙은 낚시꾼이 떠올라서였다.
150|
151|“노 선배께서는 어찌 되셨느냐.”
152|
153|내심 짐작은 하고 있으나, 그래도 놈의 입으로 직접 듣고 싶었다.
154|
155|땅바닥에 나뒹굴고 있는 저 묵빛 낚싯대의 주인이, 태원진가를 위해 기꺼이 목숨을 걸고 나서 준 동정어옹이 어찌 되었는지.
156|
157|그리고, 불길한 예감은 늘 빗나가는 법이 없다.
158|
159|“아, 그 늙은이.”
160|
161|칭겐이 흐릿한 웃음과 함께 말을 이었다.
162|
163|“낚는 솜씨는 제법이었는데, 힘이 부족했어. 분수에 안 맞는 큰 걸 낚아 버리는 바람에 그대로 부러져 버렸지. 저 낚싯대처럼.”
164|
165|“……!”
166|
167|“아니, 부러진 정도가 아니라 으스러졌겠군. 자그마치 삼십여 장 아래로 처박혔으니.”
168|
169|진위경은 침음성을 삼켰다.
170|
171|검붉은 핏물에 흠뻑 젖은, 군데군데 균열이 간 흑목조간은 동정어옹이 얼마나 치열하게 싸웠는지 알려 주는 증거였다.
172|
173|자신이 죽으면 푸른 강물에 유골을 뿌려 달라며 입버릇처럼 말했던 늙은 낚시꾼은 오늘, 바로 이 잿빛 협곡에서 뼈를 묻었다.
174|
175|태원진가에 빚진 목숨을 태원진가를 위해 내던지며.
176|
177|그리고 이제는 태원진가가 그에게 갚을 빚이 생겼다.
178|
179|동정어옹뿐만 아니라, 지금까지 죽어 간 모든 이들을 향한 빚이.
180|
181|“이름과 별호를 대라.”
182|
183|“뭐?”
184|
185|“네놈의 정체를 알아야, 훗날 망자들을 위한 제를 올릴 때 당당하게 말할 수 있지 않겠느냐.”
186|
187|진위경이 서늘한 눈빛으로 칭겐을 응시하며 말을 이었다.
188|
189|“감히 산서성을 침범하고 당신들을 해한 그 개새끼를, 우리가 직접 찢어 죽였노라고.”
190|
191|“……!”
192|
193|“제아무리 세상이 개같이 돌아간다 한들, 그것이 사람 된 도리가 아니겠느냐?”
194|
195|크게 뜬 두 눈을 깜빡이던 칭겐이, 문득 크게 소리 내어 웃었다.
196|
197|“으하, 으하하하하!”
198|
199|쩌렁쩌렁하게 울려 퍼진 웃음소리가 사방을 짓눌렀다.
200|
201|아니, 그것은 더 이상 단순한 소리라 부를 수 있는 것이 아니었다.
202|
203|우웅. 드드드득!
204|
205|부풀어 오르는 공기.
206|
207|막강한 압력과 함께 지진이라도 난 것처럼 땅과 절벽이 뒤흔들렸고, 참지 못한 신음이 곳곳에서 새어 나왔다.
208|
209|“흡……!”
210|
211|만약 거인의 손아귀에 붙잡힌다면 이런 기분일까.
212|
213|앙천대소(仰天大笑)에 실린 거대한 기운에 가까이에 있던 사람들이 중심을 잃고 비틀거렸다.
214|
215|공력이 일천한 하급 무인들 중에는 창백한 얼굴로 토혈(吐血)하는 이마저 있었다.
216|
217|“초, 초절정 고수……!”
218|
219|누군가의 입술 사이로 탄식처럼 흘러나온 한 마디. 그 안에 담긴 경악의 감정이 모두의 마음을 대변한다.
220|
221|아니, 그것으로도 부족했다.
222|
223|수십 개의 산봉우리에도 높낮이의 차이가 존재하듯이, 칭겐의 모습을 한 눈앞의 사내 역시 초절정이란 말로 다 설명할 수 있는 자가 아니었다.
224|
225|스아아아아.
226|
227|그 순간, 산서성의 무인들은 자신들의 눈을 의심했다.
228|
229|마치 보이지 않는 실과 연결된 것처럼, 여기저기 깨지고 부서진 암석의 파편이 허공에 떠오르고 있었다.
230|
231|그 숫자가 무려 백여 개.
232|
233|뾰족한 단면은 그 자체로 암기와 같았고, 그 중심에 우뚝 선 사내의 모습은 괴물이나 다름없었다.
234|
235|실로 변화무쌍한, 인간의 거죽을 뒤집어쓴 괴물.
236|
237|우둑. 뿌드드득!
238|
239|뼈가 어긋나고 살이 짓눌리는 섬뜩한 소리와 함께 시시각각 변해가는 모습.
240|
241|모두가 그 놀라운 광경을 멍하니 바라만 보고 있던 그때, 어디선가 세 줄기의 섬광이 번뜩였다.
242|
243|슈확!
244|
245|갈라지는 바람.
246|
247|케식들조차 제때에 미처 반응하지 못할 만큼, 한 줄기의 벼락이 되어 공간을 가로지른 세 사람은 약속이라도 한 것처럼 동시에 출수(出手)했다.
248|
249|후웅, 쉭!
250|
251|거력이 실린 일권(一拳)과 두 자루의 검신이 휘황한 빛줄기를 내뿜으며 칭겐을 향해 쇄도한 그 순간.
252|
253|“감히!”
254|
255|콰아아앙!
256|
257|노호성과 함께 용암처럼 터져 나온 거대한 기운이 주위의 모든 것을 밀어 냈다.
258|
259|미친 듯이 휘몰아치는 광풍과 함께.
260|
261|화아아악!
262|
263|한 치 앞도 내다볼 수 없을 만큼 희뿌연 먼지구름.
264|
265|항거할 수 없는 힘에 부딪혀 삼 장에 달하는 거리를 밀려난 세 사람이 깊게 가라앉은 눈빛으로 서로를 바라보던 그때.
266|
267|퍼엉!
268|
269|날카로운 파공성과 함께 칭겐이, 아니 그 누구도 본 적 없는 생소한 누군가가 모습을 드러냈다.
270|
271|쿵.
272|
273|묵직한 발걸음.
274|
275|어지간한 장정 두셋을 합친 것만큼이나 비대한 체구를 지닌 노인은, 이마에 맺힌 땀을 소매로 훔치며 중얼거렸다.
276|
277|“빌어먹을, 이건 도무지 적응이 안 된단 말이지.”
278|
279|조금 전까지만 하더라도 칭겐이라 불렸던 그는 오랜만에 되찾은 자신의 얼굴과 당장이라도 터질 듯한 살집을 더듬었다.
280|

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

There was no mistake. The eyes drunk on killing intent. The corners of his mouth lifted in a lazy smile. The scent of blood seeping from his entire body was so strong it stung Mukyung’s nose just to stand before him.

[P8]
*What… is this bastard?*

[P9]
Mukyung watched him, his gaze steady.

[P10]
He could feel it in his skin. He understood it in his mind. This new enemy was nothing like an ordinary villain.

[P11]
Even Pung Yang, the Red Wind Band Leader who had once raided the Mount Heng Sword Sect and inflicted a serious internal injury on Mukyung with his unexpected martial prowess, seemed like a mere mounted bandit beside this man.

[P12]
A different breed. A different class.

[P13]
In the lives he had taken, and in his martial prowess.

[P14]
Chinggen looked back at Mukyung and grinned.

[P15]
“Just as I thought. You’ve got good eyes.”

[P16]
*Step. Whish!*

[P17]
Chinggen took a light step, as though out for a stroll. Mukyung instantly sprang back and raised his sword at an angle.

[P18]
“Your Qi Sense is good, too.”

[P19]
Chinggen nodded with satisfaction.

[P20]
He had let only the faintest trace of killing intent slip, yet the young man had reacted without an instant’s hesitation.

[P21]
Enemy though he was, Chinggen liked the young Sword Demon more than he had expected. It almost seemed a waste to treat him as mere prey.

[P22]
“You’re as gloomy as an old man on his last legs, but you’re still just a brat… Who are you? Want to be my Disciple?”

[P23]
No one had expected that. The battlefield, briefly stilled by Chinggen’s arrival, stirred with alarm.

[P24]
The hundred or so nomads groaning among the fallen rocks were especially stunned. They stared wide-eyed at their Great Chieftain, hardly believing what they had heard.

[P25]
They belonged to the western grasslands ruled by Temur and Chinggen. They knew both young Great Chieftains well, which made the offer all the harder to believe.

[P26]
Chinggen had become Khan through strategy and leadership rather than personal martial prowess. Yet here he was, offering to take as a Disciple the man who, through extraordinary martial skill, had single-handedly slaughtered hundreds of their brothers from the grasslands.

[P27]
“K-Khan!”

[P28]
“What are you saying…?!”

[P29]
Shocked cries rang out on every side. The relief they had felt at the arrival of Chinggen and the Keshik was long gone.

[P30]
Chinggen smacked his lips as he looked at the injured nomads staring up at him.

[P31]
“Come to think of it, this is a strange time to make the offer, isn’t it? Especially with people watching.”

[P32]
The short sword in his left hand blurred.

[P33]
*Shk. Rrrrrumble!*

[P34]
A cold slicing sound rang out. The pile of rocks, barely holding together, collapsed onto the nomads.

[P35]
Their screams were swallowed by the roar and then vanished altogether.

[P36]
“Useless things. Never any help, but they sure do run their mouths.”

[P37]
“……!”

[P38]
“Now that no one’s watching, let’s get back to our conversation. Hmm?”

[P39]
In the sudden silence, Mukyung fixed Chinggen with a steady gaze.

[P40]
“You’re Chinggen?”

[P41]
“Hey, now. Is that any way to address me?”

[P42]
Chinggen clicked his tongue.

[P43]
“You may be a brat, but that’s no way to speak to your Master. I ought to rip your tongue out.”

[P44]
The swaggering manner. The ease of a man certain of his strength.

[P45]
Mukyung had little trouble seeing that the man before him, wearing a nomad’s distinctive hairstyle, was hiding a great many secrets.

[P46]
“You’ve disguised yourself. Where’s the real Chinggen?”

[P47]
Chinggen thought for a moment.

[P48]
“Who knows? Probably inside an eagle’s belly by now.”

[P49]
“And the other one?”

[P50]
“The other one? Oh, I left Temur alive. Had to keep one of them around to control the westerners.”

[P51]
He answered without hesitation.

[P52]
The Keshik controlled everything within several dozen *jang*. Jamukha had spent years raising them as his personal guard, and they would never betray their master.

[P53]
Even the fiercest hunting dog did not bite its owner.

[P54]
“Well, that should satisfy your curiosity. What do you say to my generous offer?”

[P55]
Chinggen looked at Mukyung expectantly.

[P56]
“Impossible.”

[P57]
A low voice cut in. Chinggen frowned at the face he saw over Mukyung’s shoulder.

[P58]
“Impossible? Why? No, first—who the hell are you?”

[P59]
The uninvited guest answered calmly.

[P60]
“How could a wolf serve under a dog? I’ve cherished my little brother like a son. As his older brother, I can’t stand by and watch that happen.”

[P61]
“Little brother? Older brother?”

[P62]
Chinggen’s eyes widened slightly as he looked at Jin Wikyung. Then he let out a short laugh.

[P63]
“The Jin brothers… This is a much bigger catch than I expected.”

[P64]
*A catch.*

[P65]
Wikyung’s gaze grew heavy. He remembered the old fisherman who had laughed before the battle and promised to bring back a big one.

[P66]
“What happened to Senior?”

[P67]
He had his suspicions, but he wanted to hear it from Chinggen himself.

[P68]
What had become of the Dongting Fisherman, who had willingly risked his life for the Jin Family of Taiyuan? Of the owner of that dark fishing rod lying on the ground?

[P69]
His worst fears were seldom wrong.

[P70]
“Oh, that old man.”

[P71]
Chinggen smiled faintly.

[P72]
“He was a decent fisherman, but he wasn’t strong enough. Hooked something too big for him and snapped. Just like that rod.”

[P73]
“……!”

[P74]
“No, ‘snapped’ isn’t quite right. More like crushed. He fell a good thirty *jang* or so.”

[P75]
Wikyung swallowed a groan.

[P76]
The black-wood fishing rod, soaked in dark red blood and cracked in several places, showed how fiercely the Dongting Fisherman had fought.

[P77]
The old fisherman had often said that when he died, he wanted his remains scattered in a blue river. Today, he had laid his bones in this gray gorge instead.

[P78]
He had given his life for the Jin Family of Taiyuan, repaying the life he owed them.

[P79]
Now the Jin Family owed him a debt. Him, and everyone else who had died here.

[P80]
“Give me your name and title.”

[P81]
“What?”

[P82]
“When we hold rites for the dead, I want to be able to tell them who you were.”

[P83]
Wikyung met Chinggen’s eyes with a cold gaze.

[P84]
“To tell them we tore apart the bastard who dared invade Shanxi Province and harm them.”

[P85]
“……!”

[P86]
“No matter how rotten the world gets, isn’t that what people ought to do?”

[P87]
Chinggen blinked, then burst into laughter.

[P88]
“Ha! Hahahahaha!”

[P89]
His laughter boomed across the gorge, pressing down on everything around him.

[P90]
No—it was no longer mere sound.

[P91]
*Vrrrrm. Rrrrattle!*

[P92]
The air swelled. An immense pressure shook the ground and cliffs as though an earthquake had struck, drawing groans from all around.

[P93]
“Urgh…!”

[P94]
Was this what it felt like to be caught in a giant’s grasp?

[P95]
The tremendous qi carried in Chinggen’s laughter made those nearby stagger. Some of the lower-level martial artists, whose internal energy was meager, went pale and coughed up blood.

[P96]
“A Supreme Peak master…!”

[P97]
The words slipped from someone’s lips like a groan. They gave voice to everyone’s shock.

[P98]
And yet even that did not go far enough.

[P99]
Just as mountain peaks differed in height, the man wearing Chinggen’s face could not be fully described by the words *Supreme Peak*.

[P100]
*Sssssss.*

[P101]
The martial artists of Shanxi Province could hardly believe their eyes.

[P102]
Fragments of broken rock were rising into the air as though suspended on invisible threads. There were a hundred or so of them.

[P103]
Their sharp edges made each fragment a hidden weapon in its own right. The man standing amid them was nothing less than a monster.

[P104]
A monster capable of endless change, wearing a human skin.

[P105]
*Crack. Crrrunch!*

[P106]
Bone shifted and flesh compressed with sickening sounds. His appearance changed by the moment.

[P107]
While everyone stared, three streaks of light flashed from somewhere nearby.

[P108]
*Shwaaa!*

[P109]
The air split.

[P110]
Three figures crossed the space like lightning, too fast for even the Keshik to react. As though they had planned it, all three struck at once.

[P111]
*Whoom. Whish!*

[P112]
A mighty punch and two gleaming blades rushed toward Chinggen—

[P113]
“How dare you!”

[P114]
*KABOOM!*

[P115]
With an enraged shout, an enormous surge of qi erupted like lava, driving everything around him away. A violent gale whipped through the gorge.

[P116]
*Fwoooooosh!*

[P117]
Pale dust filled the air, hiding everything beyond arm’s reach.

[P118]
The irresistible force had pushed the three attackers back three *jang*. They exchanged steady looks—

[P119]
*Pop!*

[P120]
A sharp crack cut through the air, and Chinggen appeared before them.

[P121]
No. Not Chinggen. Someone none of them had ever seen.

[P122]
*Thud.*

[P123]
A heavy footstep.

[P124]
The old man was as bulky as two or three ordinary men put together. He wiped the sweat from his brow with his sleeve and muttered, “Damn it. I just can’t get used to this.”

[P125]
The man who had been called Chinggen moments ago felt his own face, restored after so long, then the flesh that seemed ready to burst from his body.

[P126]
Old and ugly.

[P127]
That alone was unpleasant enough. Being ambushed while enduring the painful reversal of his disguise technique and Bone-Shrinking Technique had made his mood far worse.

[P128]
“The nerve of you ungrateful bastards…”

[P129]
He glared at the rats who had dared attack him. His eyes were so narrow and buried in fat they were barely visible.

[P130]
He was furious—especially because Jin Mukyung, the first person in a long while to catch his interest, was among them.

[P131]
“You dared ambush your Master? You’re expelled.”

[P132]
At the old man’s declaration, Mukyung found himself wondering how his troublesome younger brother would have answered such nonsense if he were here.

[P133]
Then he came up with a likely answer.

[P134]
“Go suck a dog’s dick.”

[P135]
“……!”

[P136]
“Oh. And you’re a pig bastard, too.”

[P137]
The old man’s eyes reddened with rage. Reflected in them were the two men smiling on either side of Mukyung.

[P138]
“And who are you?”

[P139]
The two men, one young and one old, answered readily.

[P140]
“Ghost Sword Wipeng.”

[P141]
“Tiger of Mount Heng, Cheol Mubaek.”

[P142]
At the answers of the two Peak masters representing the Jin Family of Taiyuan and the Mount Heng Sword Sect, the old man licked his lips with a tongue surprisingly quick for his size.

[P143]
“One about to become a ghost, and a dog from Mount Heng. Good to know.”

[P144]
*Shing.*

[P145]
Metal scraped coldly against metal. The old man crossed the two swords in his hands.

[P146]
“When you reach the underworld, tell them the Demon Bird sent you.”

[P147]
Those words were the signal.

[P148]
The battlefield’s suspended moment ended, and the wick that had barely kept burning caught in a blood-red blaze.

[P149]
“Waaaaaah!”

[P150]
A great roar shattered the deep night as two waves crashed into each other.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.

- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.

- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.

- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.

- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
